JUDGMENT
The Police Inspector of Kengeri P.S has submitted the Charge Sheet against the accused No.1 & 2 for the offences punishable U/S.498, 506 of IPC and 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act 1961.

2. The brief facts of the Prosecution case are as follows:
That on 23.12.2010, complainant married to accused no.1 at C sector convention center situated at Tiruvanapalli, Tamilnadu and at the time of marriage, accused had received golden ornaments of Rs.5,00,000/-.

After the marriage, when CW-1 and accused were residing at plot no.10, 3rd street, Gandhi Salai, Kilash nagar,
Tiruchanapalli, Tamilnadu-620019, at that time the accused demanded to CW-1 to bring additional dowry and pushed her out from the house.

Further on 30-11-2012 at about 07.00 Am, accused came to the house of CW-2 situated at no.999/2, 1st cross,
Biravanagara, Dubasipalya, R.V.college post, Bengaluru-59 and picked up quarrel with CW-1, assaulted her and gave life threat if she does not bring additional dowry and thereby the accused No.1 & 2 have committed the offences punishable U/S.498A,
506 of IPC and 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
3. On the basis of the Statement of CW1, the Kengeri Police have registered a case under Crime No.04/2013 for the offences punishable U/S.498A, 506 of IPC, 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act against the accused No.1 & 2 and submitted the FIR before the court.

Thereafter investigating officer visited the spot and drawn the spot mahazar and recorded the statement of witnesses on completion of the investigation, the Charge Sheet has been filed against the accused 1 & 2 for the offences punishable U/S.498A, 506 of IPC and section 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
On the receipt of the police report, this court has taken cognizance for the said offences.
4. On the appearance of the accused No.1 & 2, the accused No.1 & 2 surrendered before court and were released on bail.

The copies of prosecution papers were furnished to the accused No.1 & 2 as The State Through vs Riyaz Ahamad on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179988224/
2 contemplated U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. After hearing both the parties
, the charge was framed against the accused No.1& 2 for the offences punishable U/S.498A, 506 of IPC and 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
Accused No.1 & 2 pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
Hence, the matter was posted for evidence.

5. In order to bring home the guilt of the accused No.1 and 2, the prosecution has got examined one witness as PW-1, out of total charge sheet witnesses as CW-1 to 10 and got marked 2 documents as Ex.P1 with sub markings.

Since PW-1 who is the material witness, has turned hostile to the case of the prosecution and the presence of rest of the material witnesses could not be secured and since there is no incriminating evidence against the accused persons from the material witness, no purpose would be served by issuing summons to rest of the witnesses.
Hence, the evidence of rest of the witnesses is dropped by rejecting the prayer of the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor.
The statement of the accused as required Under Sec.313 of Cr.P.C was dispensed with as there was no incriminating circumstances in the evidence of prosecution witnesses.
6. I have heard the arguments addressed by the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor and learned advocate for the accused.

7. On going through the facts and circumstances of the prosecution case, the following points would arise for my consideration :
POINTS 1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on 23-12-2010,
accused No.1 married with CW-1 and at the time of marriage, accused along with accused no.2 instigated and demanded and taken gold worth Rs.5,00,000/- cash as dowry and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act?
2.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that when CW1 was residing with accused in her matrimonial house, at that time accused assaulted with hands to CW-1 and demanded to bring additional dowry thereby gave physical and mental cruelty and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s 498(A) of IPC?

3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused along with accused no.2 has threatened CW-1 with dire consequences and thereby accused has committed an offence punishable u/s 506 of IPC?
4. What Order?

8. My findings to the above Points are as under:
 Points No.1 to 3 : In the Negative.
 Point No.4 :

As per final order,

Points No.1 to 3 :- As these points are interlinked with each other and also similar evidence is led on all these points, I have taken all these points together for common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts and discussion.

10. It is the allegation that the accused No.1 & 2 have committed the offences punishable U/S.498A,
506 of IPC and 3 & 4 of DP Act,
11.

In order to prove its case, prosecution has got examined informant of crime/C.W.1 by name Smt.Ayisha Tabasum as PW.1.
12.
Out of the documents marked for the prosecution Ex.P1 is the complaint, Ex.P2 is the spot mahazar.
13. In support of the case of prosecution, C.W.1-informant by name Smt.Ayisha Tubsum is examined as P.W.1.
This witness deposed that accused No.1 is her husband and her marriage was solemnized on 23.12.2010.

She further deposed that during her stay with the accused at matrimonial home, the accused persons have not demanded additional dowry, not given physical, mental cruelty and not abused in filthy language and not threatened and she has not lodged complaint against the accused persons and police took her signature on blank papers and police have not drawn mahazar in her presence and she does not know the contents of Ex.P.1- complaint and Ex.P.2-Mahazar.
14. This witness was treated as hostile witness by the Learned Sr.Asst.Public Prosecutor and cross examined at length.

In the cross examination also nothing worth could be elicited from her mouth to support the case of the prosecution and she denied the suggestion that she is deposing false evidence in view of compromising the matter with the accused persons.
15. Now the question which arises before the court is whether the evidence placed on record is sufficient to establish the case of the prosecution.
As I have above stated, the prime witness P.W.1 fully turned hostile to the case of the prosecution.

After appreciating the evidence placed on record,
it is clear that the evidence of P.W.1 is not inspiring confidence to act upon and to hold that the accused persons committed the alleged offences.
16. Now on overall perusal of the evidence and prosecution witness as complainant/PW-1.
PW-1 is the material witness has not supported the case of the prosecution.

The PW-1 during the course of her evidence has not at all stated in respect of abuse, assault and harassment against C.W.1 and threat by the accused persons and she has denied the involvement of the accused persons and at the out set she has denied the entire case of the prosecution.
17. However, the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor prays to issue summons to other witnesses.

Having considered the facts and circumstances of this case, this court was of the opinion that even if The State Through vs Riyaz Ahamad on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179988224/
4 other witnesses were examined, it would be a futile excise and no lawful purpose would have been served.

As such examination of the prosecution witnesses only for the purpose of completing the procedural aspect and will not serve any judicial purpose and it is sheer waste of the precious time of the court.
Therefore, the prayer of the learned APP to issue summons to other witnesses was rejected.

At this stage this court relied upon judgment delivered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 1996 (3) Crimes 84 Sathish Mehra V/s Delhi Administration & another: wherein at page No.13 the Hon'ble Apex Court held as follows:
"When the judge is fairly certain that there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction the valuable time of the court should not be wasted for holding a trial only for the purpose of formally completing the procedure to pronounce the conclusion on the future date".

entities.text: 1996 (3) Crimes 84 Sathish Mehra V/s Delhi Administration
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 18. The principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above case is applicable in this case also.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, it is clear that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused persons beyond all reasonable doubts.

Under these facts and circumstances of the case, the above Points No.1 to 3 is answered in the 'NEGATIVE'.
19. Point No.4: - In view of the findings of points No.1 to 3, this Court proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/Sec.248 (1) of Cr.P.C. accused No.1 & 2 are acquitted of the offences punishable U/S.498A, 506 of IPC and 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act 1961.
and Surety bonds shall stand canceled.
Section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. has been complied.
